method: Executed browser/Playwright checks against the actual local application, plus six focused code-label/marker-key unit tests and the existing model regression suite.

checks.check: Visible code in every destination card
checks.observed: Five titles explicitly read Location P/A/B/C/X followed by the corresponding existing destination name.
The default-open key lists H,P,A,B,C,X with names; H is explained as fixed origin/return, not a selectable destination, and X appears only for custom selection.

checks.check: Original choices match selected marker identity
checks.observed: Selecting each P/A/B/C changes the caption to its Location code and highlights the same code in the marker key.
The internal selector value custom is not used as a map code; custom choice uses Location X in card, caption and selected key.
At actual 390 x 844 CSS viewport, document width remains 375 px without horizontal overflow.
The native radio is discoverable by Location P plus its name, and Activities retains the same explicit location code.
Guided P still produces 61.92 min extra margin under unchanged model inputs.
Printed brief content names origin/return H and Location P; result JSON retains destination id P and all H/P/A/B/C/X marker definitions.

checks.check: Original A and fixed origin preserved
checks.observed: A still returns NO_MODELED_ROUTE with null time at the nominal setting; origin remains row 105, column 43.

limitations: This is a destination-label and map-key correction, not a scientific renaming or change to positions, durations, routing, safety constraints or real-world site validation.
The 1.1.0 browser record and 1.1.1 layer checks remain historical evidence; they are not falsely presented as complete fresh reruns.
No human usability pilot, actual Rumahweb deployment or new physical/operational validation was performed.
